text: Complements, independence, conditional probability.

An event (事件) is a set of outcomes. P(A) is its probability; P(not A) = 1 − P(A); for disjoint events probabilities add; for independent events they multiply. The conditional probability P(A | B) = P(A and B) / P(B) is the probability of A once we know B happened.

Conditional problems become counting: restrict to the outcomes where B holds, and measure how much of that weight also has A. With n ≤ 20 independent people you can simply enumerate all 2ⁿ outcomes as bitmasks (第17章).
Case 1:
Probability | Given (UVA11181): each friend buys independently with probability pi; we are told exactly r bought. P(i bought | r bought) = P(i bought and exactly r bought) / P(exactly r bought).
Exactly two of three buy with weight 0.1·0.2·0.7 + 0.1·0.8·0.3 + 0.9·0.2·0.3 = 0.092; friend 1 is in the first two: (0.014 + 0.024) / 0.092 ≈ 0.413.
Classical model; write it down first.

A probability model (概率模型) fixes what is random and how. Classical: finitely many equally likely outcomes, P = good / all. Geometric: a point uniform in a region, P = good area / total area. Most contest problems are classical: count, then divide.
Write the model down before computing: "question i is answered with the correct answer of question i − 1, which is uniform among ai−1 options". A wrong model gives a confident wrong answer.

Shifted answers (P1297): question i has ai options and its true answer is uniform; the written answer is the true answer of question i − 1. Both are uniform and independent, and they can only agree on the smaller range: P = min / (ai·ai−1) = 1 / max(ai, ai−1).

Expected number correct = Σ P(question i correct): linearity of expectation (21.3) lets you add the per- question probabilities even though the questions are not independent. The real problem generates a with a formula; the idea is unchanged.
Linearity and indicators; expected powers of a combo.
node 4 is removed by itself iff it is picked before its ancestors 3 and 1: probability 1 / depth = 1/3

The expected value (数学期望) E[X] = Σ x·P(X = x). Its most useful property: linearity, E[X + Y] = E[X] + E[Y] for any X, Y, even dependent ones. So split the quantity into small pieces (indicators: 1 if something happens, 0 otherwise) and add the probabilities.
Game on a tree (CF280C): each step removes a random remaining node with its subtree; expected number of steps?
Steps = Σ [node i is picked itself]. Node i is picked itself exactly when it is the first chosen among its depth(i) ancestors-or-self, each equally likely: E = Σ 1 / depth(i).
Two nodes in a line: the root is always picked itself (1), the child only if picked first (1/2): 1.5. A root with two leaves: 1 + 1/2 + 1/2 = 2.
No probability of "the game lasts k steps" was ever computed: linearity skips the whole distribution. That is the usual way to solve expectation problems.

title: Expectations that need more than linearity

text: Score = Σ (combo length)²: add the increase each click makes, (L + 1)² − L² = 2L + 1, which is linear in L, so only E[L] is needed (P1365). For L³ the increase 3L² + 3L + 1 needs E[L²] too, which is kept with the same trick one level down (P1654 OSU!).
E[L²] ≠ (E[L])². Squares and products of random variables need their own expectations; only sums split freely.

Expectation DPs: the frog on a DAG (P4316, 第16章) fills f backwards from the end; changing classrooms (P1850) is a DP over (class, requests used, last request made?) where each step adds expected walking distances from Floyd. Write E as a recurrence over what is still to come, not over what has happened.
The Luogu problems for this chapter, a ladder through them, and experiments to try yourself.
Key points to memorise
1. P(not A) = 1 − P(A); independent: multiply; disjoint: add.
2. P(A | B) = P(A and B) / P(B): restrict to B, then measure A.
3. Classical model: good / all; write the model down first.
4. Linearity: E[X + Y] = E[X] + E[Y], always. Split into indicators.
5. Tree game: node removed itself with probability 1 / depth.
6. Combo²: add 2L + 1 per hit; keep E[L].
7. Combo³: add 3L² + 3L + 1; keep E[L] and E[L²].
8. E[L²] ≠ E[L]²; expectation DPs run backwards over what is still to come.
